It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and its former {{ill|Shakaku|ja|社格|ko|사격 (신토)|zh|社格|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}. {{nihongo|'''Sogahime Shrine'''|蘇我比咩神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}. It is located in {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ckb|پارێزگای شیمۆسا|cs|Provincie Šimósa|de|Provinz Shimousa|es|Provincia de Shimōsa|fa|ولایت شیموسا|fr|Province de Shimōsa|gl|Provincia de Shimōsa|hak|Shimōsa-koet|id|Provinsi Shimousa|it|Shimōsa|ja|下総国|ko|시모사국|lt|Šimosos žemė|nl|Shimosa (provincie)|pt|Província de Shimōsa|ru|Симоса (провинция)|simple|Shimōsa Province|sk|Šimósa|sr|Провинција Шимоса|tr|Shimōsa (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Сімоса|zh|下總國|zh_min_nan|Simôsa-kok|zh_yue|下總國|qid=Q1053695|lt=Shimōsa Province}}.

The principal enshrined deities are Sogahime Ōkami and Chiyoharu Inari Ōkami. In the medieval period, the Kasuga deities became the center of worship, and the shrine was called Kasuga Daimyōjin.

== History ==
The date of founding is unknown. According to the myths recorded in the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki, when {{ill|Yamato Takeru|arz|ياماتو تاكيرو|be|Ямата Такэру|de|Yamatotakeru|es|Yamato Takeru|fa|یاماتو تاکه‌رو|fr|Yamato Takeru|hu|Jamatotakeru|id|Yamato Takeru|it|Yamato Takeru|ja|ヤマトタケル|ko|야마토타케루|pt|Yamato Takeru|ru|Ямато Такэру|sh|Yamato Takeru|simple|Yamato Takeru|sq|Jamato Takeru|sr|Јамато Такеру|sv|Yamato Takeru|tr|Yamato Takeru|uk|Ямато Такеру|ur|یاماتو تاکیرو|vi|Yamato Takeru|zh|日本武尊|zh_min_nan|Yamato Takeru|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru no Mikoto}} was on his eastern campaign and attempted to cross from Sagami to Fusa Province, he encountered a violent storm. To calm it, his consort {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Oto Tachibana-hime}} threw herself into the sea. According to shrine tradition, five women who had accompanied Oto Tachibana-hime also entered the water with her. Of these, only Sogahime, the daughter of a Soga minister, was washed ashore, where she was cared for by villagers, revived, and returned to the capital. Later, when the villagers heard that Yamato Takeru had died on his way back, they built a shrine to console his spirit. {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ar|الإمبراطور أوجين|arz|الامبراطور اوجين|azb|اوجین (ایمپیراتور)|bn|সম্রাট ওজিন|cs|Ódžin|de|Ōjin|es|Ōjin Tennō|eu|Ōjin enperadorea|fa|امپراتور اوجین|fi|Ōjin|fr|Ōjin|hr|Ōjin|id|Kaisar Ōjin|it|Ōjin|ja|応神天皇|ka|ოძინი|ko|오진 천황|nl|Ojin|pl|Ōjin|pt|Ojin|ru|Император Одзин|sh|Car Ōjin|simple|Emperor Ōjin|sl|Cesar Odžin|sv|Ojin|th|จักรพรรดิโอจิง|tl|Emperador Ōjin|tr|Ōjin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Одзін|uz|Imperator Ōjin|vi|Thiên hoàng Ōjin|yo|Emperor Ōjin|zh|应神天皇|zh_min_nan|Ôzin Thian-hông|zh_yue|應神天皇|qid=Q317997}} was deeply moved by this act and appointed the {{ill|Soga clan|ar|سوغا (عشيرة)|ca|Clan Soga|de|Soga (Klan)|es|Clan Soga|fa|خاندان سوگا|fi|Soga-klaani|fr|Clan Soga|hr|Soga (klan)|hu|Szoga klán|id|Klan Soga|it|Clan Soga|ja|蘇我氏|ko|소가씨|nl|Soga|pl|Soga (ród)|pt|Clã Soga|ru|Сога (род)|sh|Soga (klan)|tr|Soga boyu|uk|Рід Соґа|vi|Gia tộc Soga|zh|蘇我氏|qid=Q909854}} as {{ill|Kuni no miyatsuko|es|Kuni no miyatsuko|ff|Kuni no miyatsuko|it|Kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造|ko|국조 (일본)|simple|Kuni no miyatsuko|vi|Kuni no miyatsuko|zh|國造|qid=Q2483673}} of the surrounding area. The Soga clan revered {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|ca|Gran santuari de Kasuga|co|Grandi Santuariu Kasuga|cs|Svatyně Kasuga|de|Kasuga-Taisha|es|Kasuga-taisha|eu|Kasuga-taisha|fa|کاسوگا-تایشا|fi|Kasuga-taisha|fr|Kasuga-taisha|he|מקדש קאסוגה|id|Kuil Agung Kasuga|it|Santuario Kasuga|ja|春日大社|ka|კასუგა-ტაისია|ko|가스가타이샤|la|Kasuga-taisha|pl|Kasuga Taisha|pt|Kasuga-taisha|ru|Касуга тайся|sh|Kasuga-taisha|simple|Kasuga Taisha|sl|Svetišče Kasuga|th|ศาลเจ้าคาซูงะ|tok|tomo sewi suli Kasuka|tr|Kasuga-taisha|uk|Касуга тайся|zh|春日大社|qid=Q714559}} and Hime Shrine, and it is said that they invited the deities of both shrines and founded Sogahime Shrine.

However, there is another tradition: it was Oto Tachibana-hime herself who was washed ashore and revived, and because she said “I have revived (yo-mi-gaeri),” the place name “Soga” is said to have originated from this phrase.
